basis: Distal joint contractures and congenital hand and foot deformities define this arthrogryposis.
Invasive Candida infection; anatomical sites vary, with no additional organ established as commonly damaged across the group.
Congenital postaxial polydactyly affects the skeletal structure of hands and feet.
Congenital duplication of the stomach.
Malignant embryonal tumour arising in the liver; associated syndromes and metastatic risks do not add axes.
Inherited platelet adhesion and aggregation dysfunction causing abnormal bleeding.
Marfanoid skeletal connective-tissue abnormalities and aortic disease characterize the group; damaging ocular involvement is subtype-dependent and not established at >=30% group-wide.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%, with hand and finger contractures in 30-79%, supporting lasting musculoskeletal involvement.
MAN1B1 glycosylation disorder with intellectual disability; cutis laxa 5/7 and strabismus 5/12 support skin and eye involvement. Joint hypermobility 7/19 omitted at cap.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; intellectual disability affects 26/33. Common renal damage is not established for this subtype.
Autoinflammatory syndrome establishes immune-mediated disease; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to another organ.
Necrotizing bacterial infection of soft tissues, including skin, subcutis, fascia and skeletal muscle.
Congenital absence of the tricuspid valve with right ventricular hypoplasia and associated cardiac or great-vessel malformations.
Intellectual developmental disorder with ataxia; elevated LDL in 2/2 supports lipid involvement and developmental cataract in 1/3 meets the ocular threshold, with small samples.
CNS hypomyelination with basal ganglia and cerebellar degeneration; documented ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Impaired corneal trophic innervation causes corneal epithelial injury and keratoconjunctivitis; an additional neurologic disease is not intrinsic.
Obstructive cyst of a female reproductive vestibular gland; this anatomical site has no axis.
Congenital skeletal myofibril disease; dysphagia (3/10) and reduced FVC reflect muscle dysfunction without established direct gut or lung damage. Aortic coarctation occurs in 2/10.
Telomere-related disease defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or hypocellular bone marrow failure.
Tyrosine metabolism disorder defined by corneal disease and palmoplantar keratoderma; intellectual disability is annotated at 80-99%.
Creatine transport defect with cerebral dysfunction; intestinal motility failure is annotated at 30-79%, and prolonged QT in 7/18 supports cardiac electrical dysfunction.
Aplasia cutis and terminal limb reduction defects define the syndrome; individual cardiac defects occur in 1/5, without evidence of >=30% cardiac involvement.
Benign adipose neoplasm occupying the internal auditory canal; possible vestibulocochlear nerve adherence does not establish another axis.
Isolated developmental eye disorder combining microphthalmia and ocular coloboma.
Carcinoma arising in the sublingual salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
